title: Marginalia eval — LLM judge rubric

classMetricMapping.faithfulness: faithfulness (no unsupported textual/factual claims vs ALLOWED_EVIDENCE)
classMetricMapping.chunk_relevance: relevance of retrieved chunks to the question
classMetricMapping.answer_completeness: recall of the prompt (and fair gold points) — did the answer cover what was asked
classMetricMapping.claim_precision: precision — specificity and avoidance of vague or over-broad claims weakly tied to evidence

binaryFlags.whenOne: Set to 1 if substantive factual or textual claims are not grounded in ALLOWED_EVIDENCE (invention, fabricated quotes, wrong section references, facts not in anchor or tool excerpts). Otherwise 0.
Set to 1 if retrieved excerpts are largely off-topic, wrong locus, noisy filler, or evidence is insufficient for what the question asked (given tools/smart_scan were available or used). Otherwise 0.
Set to 1 if major sub-parts of the prompt or fair gold rubric hints are missing, evaded, or only hand-waved. Otherwise 0.
Set to 1 if the answer is generic boilerplate, hand-wavy, or claims exceed what the evidence supports (precision / over-breadth). Otherwise 0.

dimensions.definition: Every substantive factual or textual claim in the assistant answer is supported by the ALLOWED_EVIDENCE block (anchor passage + retrieved tool text). Paraphrase is fine; invention is not.

anchors.1: Contains clear hallucinations, plot/author facts, or quotations not grounded in ALLOWED_EVIDENCE.
anchors.2: Several important claims lack support or misrepresent the cited material.
anchors.3: Mostly grounded, but one or two substantive claims are weakly supported or overreach.
anchors.4: Nearly all substantive claims are well supported; any stretch is minor and hedged.
anchors.5: Rigorously grounded; interpretations are explicitly tied to specific phrases or retrieved lines.

dimensions.definition: The retrieved excerpts (tool outputs) are pertinent to the user question: they help answer it or legitimately contextualize it, without being mostly off-topic filler.

anchors.1: Retrieval is largely irrelevant or misleading for the question.
anchors.2: Some relevant material, but major portions are off-topic or the wrong locus.
anchors.3: Mixed relevance: helpful chunks alongside noticeable noise.
anchors.4: Mostly on-target; small amount of extra context is reasonable.
anchors.5: Tight, high-yield retrieval for this prompt (given what was retrieved).

dimensions.definition: The answer addresses every part of the prompt (including implicit sub-parts like 'where later…' or 'how does X relate to Y') and reflects the gold rubric points when they are fair expectations for the ALLOWED_EVIDENCE.

anchors.1: Misses the main task or most sub-parts of the question.
anchors.2: Addresses the topic but omits major requested elements.
anchors.3: Covers the core adequately; noticeable gaps on secondary asks.
anchors.4: Covers essentially all parts; only minor omissions.
anchors.5: Fully responsive, including nuanced sub-parts, without unnecessary digression.

dimensions.definition: Precision of the answer as literary analysis: avoids vague boilerplate, avoids overbroad generalizations unsupported by evidence, and does not smuggle strong claims without textual backing.

anchors.1: Mostly generic or speculative; little textual specificity.
anchors.2: Frequent vague claims; weak linkage to specifics.
anchors.4: Generally precise, with clear textual hooks.
anchors.5: Sharply precise; claims match the grain of the quoted/retrieved language.

globalRules: Score ONLY from ALLOWED_EVIDENCE and the assistant answer. Do not use private knowledge of the book beyond what appears in ALLOWED_EVIDENCE.
If ALLOWED_EVIDENCE is thin for a book-level question, do not penalize missing sections that were never retrieved—penalize only unsupported claims presented as textual fact.
Interpretation is allowed when tied to evidence; invented quotations or precise locations not present in ALLOWED_EVIDENCE are severe faithfulness failures.

If the condition is passage_only and there is no retrieved text, evaluate chunk_relevance as 5 only if no retrieval was needed; if the question clearly required elsewhere-in-book evidence and the answer supplies it without retrieval, treat unsupported book-wide factual claims as low faithfulness.
Return scores as integers on the 1–5 scale defined in this rubric.
Include binary flags: each flag id must be the integer 0 or 1 only (no booleans as strings). Set a flag to 1 only when that failure mode is clearly present.
